messages:
Lina (sales): Heads up 10AM buyer call recap: NovaGrid wants to run a 21-day POC. They attached their PO (NG-PO-78) with an escrow clause, Net60, and a tax withholding appendix. They also sent a security questionnaire link: https://sq.vendor.com/novagrid-poc. Need legal + finance + solutions signoff before sending redline.

Arjun (legal): Thanks. Can you paste the PO escrow paragraph and the tax wording? Also, do they ask to modify our MSA or just attach their PO to the order form?

Lina (sales): Escrow paragraph: "Supplier shall deposit source code into escrow and irrevocably authorize release upon Buyer insolvency or termination for convenience." Tax clause: "Buyer may withhold taxes as required; any withholdings are for Supplier's account." They attached their PO only, not an MSA.

Noah (solutions): For the POC we plan to provide a hosted sandbox (no dedicated infra), expected invoice ~$12k. We can supply reproducible artifacts + runbook. Source escrow is overkill for a short POC.

Arjun (legal): Agreed. Proposed vendor redline to buyer: narrow escrow to "compiled deliverables and operational runbooks only"; escrow release triggers limited to bankruptcy or long-term failure to support beyond an agreed 90-day transition window. Also remove "irrevocably" and require a signed 3-party escrow agreement listing the escrow agent and jurisdiction.

Maya (finance): Net60 for a $12k POC is outside standard terms. Our default POC terms are Net30 prepaid or Net15 invoice when under $15k, depending on buyer. Net60 requires director approval and increases cash collection risk. What's their payment method?

Pri (AE): Procurement noted they prefer Net60 for enterprise vendors. Payment method is their standard ACH via bank transfer.

Arjun (legal): On the tax clause: we should accept "Buyer complies with applicable tax withholding laws and will provide documentation of withholdings; any withheld amounts will be grossed up or credited to Supplier where applicable by treaty or law." Proposed concise redline: "Buyer may withhold taxes as required by law; Buyer will provide evidence and apply withholdings only to the extent required by law."

Noah (solutions): Also confirm no proprietary build scripts or private keys go into escrow. We can provide installable binaries, license keys, and runbook. If buyer insists on source-level access, escalate.

Lina (sales): I'll push back on source and Net60. Meanwhile, procurement asked if Redwood can do parallel signing via DocuSign so their legal and procurement can both sign without sequential delays.

Maya (finance): We support parallel signing flows for small POs. However, our internal policy still requires legal approval before execution. We can configure DocuSign for parallel signatures (Legal + Finance), but legal sign-off must be present in the envelope setup.

Arjun (legal): I'll prepare redline language and attach as annotated PO. Key items: limit escrow scope, require escrow agent/jurisdiction details, remove irrevocable release, tighten tax withholding wording, and deny subcontractor indemnity expansion.

DocuSign Bot: Draft envelope 2955550025 created (NovaGrid-PO NG-PO-78). Status: draft, awaiting attachments (annotated PO).

Lina (sales): ETA: I'll send annotated PO to NovaGrid now and ask if they can accept Net30 or prepayment and accept narrowed escrow scope. Copying their procurement contact (Dana).

Pri (AE): If buyer accepts Net30 + narrowed escrow, we're green. If they insist on Net60 + source escrow release, escalate to Arjun + revenue ops.

Maya (finance): Confirmed. I'll queue manager approval if they keep Net60, but call out risks to collections.

Arjun (legal): One more note: include a clause that escrow artifacts exclude CI credentials, internal third-party integrations, and monitoring dashboards. Escrow items limited to distributable runtime artifacts and install/run documentation.

Lina (sales): Thanks all. I'll update thread with NovaGrid response and attach the buyer PO and their SQ answers once received. :raised_hands:
